textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Prime Time · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: In the idli-vada game, idli is said at 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on, and vada at 5, 10, 15 and so on. The numbers that are multiples of both 3 and 5 are called common multiples, and the first of them is 15.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: In the idli-vada game, idli is said at 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on, and vada at 5, 10, 15 and so on. The numbers that are multiples of both 3 and 5 are called common multiples, and the first of them is 15.
beats.speakEn: In the idli-vada game, idli is said at 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on, and vada at 5, 10, 15 and so on. The numbers that are multiples of both 3 and 5 are called common multiples, and the first of them is 15.

beats.en: A number is a factor of another if it divides it exactly. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Each pair of factors multiplies to give 12, such as 3 x 4. Common factors are the factors shared by two numbers.
beats.speakEn: A number is a factor of another if it divides it exactly. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. Each pair of factors multiplies to give 12, such as 3 x 4. Common factors are the factors shared by two numbers.

type: Key Concept: In the idli-vada game, idli is said at 3, 6, 9, 12 and so on, and vada at 5, 10, 15 and so on.
Rule: A number is a factor of another if it divides it exactly.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 maths · Prime Time · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. The first primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

beats.en: A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. The first primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.
beats.speakEn: A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. The first primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

beats.en: Two numbers are called co-prime if they have no common factor other than 1. In the treasure game with two treasures, a pair is safe from Jumpy only if the numbers are co-prime.
beats.speakEn: Two numbers are called co-prime if they have no common factor other than 1. In the treasure game with two treasures, a pair is safe from Jumpy only if the numbers are co-prime.
